sights.n: Super Potato Akihabara (スーパーポテト 秋葉原店)
sights.address: Kitabayashi Bldg 3F–5F, 1-11-2 Sotokanda, Chiyoda City, Tokyo 〒101-0021
sights.w: Three floors of retro consoles, cartridges and memorabilia in a Mario-decorated building; Time Out calls the Akihabara flagship the chain's most famous location, 'almost like a museum'.
sights.anime: Retro video games — Akihabara's best-known shrine to Famicom/Super Famicom-era Nintendo, Sega and arcade culture

sights.n: Mandarake Complex Akihabara (まんだらけコンプレックス)
sights.w: Eight-storey flagship of the second-hand otaku chain, each floor sorted by product type — vintage 'Japanese Pop Antique' figures, magical-girl toys and cosplay, manga, dōjinshi and more (Time Out, Tokyo Cheapo).
sights.anime: Anime & manga collectibles — the biggest single Mandarake, Akihabara's deep-cut used-figure and dōjinshi tower

sights.n: The Gundam Base Tokyo (ガンダムベース東京)
sights.address: DiverCity Tokyo Plaza 7F, 1-1-10 Aomi, Kōtō City, Tokyo 〒135-0064
sights.w: Bandai's official Gunpla (Gundam plastic-model) flagship: a shop zone with 2,000+ kits on sale, a replica of the Shizuoka factory line and a builders' zone (Time Out). Keeps operating after the Unicorn Gundam statue outside retired in Aug 2026.
sights.anime: Mobile Suit Gundam — Bandai's official Gunpla HQ shop, the pilgrimage stop for model builders

sights.n: Toshima City Tokiwasō Manga Museum (豊島区立トキワ荘マンガミュージアム)
sights.w: A 2020 reconstruction of the Tokiwasō apartment where Tezuka Osamu, Fujiko Fujio and Ishinomori Shōtarō lived as young artists; the 2F recreates the 1950s–60s four-and-a-half-mat rooms and shared kitchen (GO TOKYO, japan-guide).
sights.anime: Manga history — the 'sacred place' of postwar manga where Tezuka and the Doraemon/Cyborg 009 creators started out

sights.n: Suginami Animation Museum (杉並アニメーションミュージアム)
sights.address: Suginami Kaikan 3F, 3-29-5 Kamiogi, Suginami City, Tokyo 〒167-0043
sights.w: Free museum run by Tokyo Polytechnic University in the ward with Japan's densest cluster of anime studios; history-of-anime galleries, a dubbing booth, digital workshop, theatre and library (GO TOKYO, japan-guide).
sights.anime: Anime industry — Japan's only museum devoted solely to animation, in the studio heartland of Suginami

sights.n: Suga Shrine stairs, Yotsuya (須賀神社 男坂)
sights.address: Suga Shrine (須賀神社), Sugachō, Yotsuya, Shinjuku City, Tokyo
sights.w: The stone 'Otokozaka' staircase below Suga Shrine is where Taki and Mitsuha finally meet in the last scene of Shinkai Makoto's Your Name (2016) and on its poster; nippon.com calls it among the most famous seichi-junrei sites in Japan. Nearest station Yotsuya-sanchōme.
sights.anime: Your Name. (Kimi no Na wa) — the film's final-reunion staircase and poster image

sights.n: @home cafe Akihabara Main Branch (@ほぉ〜むカフェ 本店)
sights.address: Mitsuwa Building 4F/6F/7F, Sotokanda, Chiyoda City, Tokyo (Akihabara)
sights.w: Japan's biggest and most popular maid-café chain (Time Out), with three floors of its main branch in Akihabara's Mitsuwa Building (Tokyo Cheapo); a newer flagship opened in Feb 2022 on 5F of Akiba Cultures Zone.
sights.anime: Akihabara otaku culture — the best-known maid café, the archetypal Akiba moe experience

sights.n: Pokémon Center Mega Tokyo, Ikebukuro (ポケモンセンターメガトウキョー)
sights.address: Sunshine City Alpa 2F, 3-1 Higashi-Ikebukuro, Toshima City, Tokyo
sights.w: Pokémon's biggest Tokyo store (opened Dec 2014) on the 2nd floor of Sunshine City, with a store-exclusive Mega Charizard X statue; open 10:00–20:00, near Pikachu Sweets by Pokémon Café (GO TOKYO, Time Out).
sights.anime: Pokémon — the 'Mega' flagship Pokémon Center with its exclusive Mega Charizard X statue
